findings.evidence: "The finance office reviews overdue notice counts on the first of every month. Historical figures are archived for five years before being summarized and retired."
findings.fix: Remove this paragraph, or replace it with data that actually bears on the fines decision (e.g., historical trend in overdue notice volume).
findings.violation: This fact about archival schedules has no bearing on whether to end overdue fines and is never referenced again in the argument.

findings.evidence: "The finance office reviews self-checkout usage at the end of each quarter. Branch-level totals roll up into the consortium's shared reporting dashboard."
findings.fix: Cut this paragraph, or explain how self-checkout usage connects to the fines decision if it's meant to matter.
findings.violation: Self-checkout usage is irrelevant to the fines recommendation and is never used as evidence anywhere else in the document.

findings.evidence: "the on-time-or-eventual return rate for borrowed items held at 93 percent"
findings.fix: Report on-time return rate and eventual return rate as separate figures, or report average days overdue, so the comparison isn't masked by the combined metric.
findings.location: What the Pilot Showed, first paragraph
findings.violation: "On-time-or-eventual" lumps together prompt returns and very late returns into one figure, which hides whether removing fines actually made items come back later even if they still come back eventually.

findings.evidence: "The survey was administered at the same pilot branches immediately before and twelve months into the pilot" following mention of an "18-month pilot"
findings.fix: Either administer (or cite) a survey taken at the 18-month mark, or adjust the description of the pilot length to match the period the survey actually covers.
findings.location: What the Pilot Showed, second paragraph
findings.violation: The post-pilot survey was taken at the 12-month mark, not at the end of the 18-month pilot, so the avoidance-rate improvement isn't actually measured over the full period the recommendation is based on.

findings.evidence: "the stronger choice is a systemwide end to overdue fines across all ten consortium branches"
findings.fix: Either limit the recommendation's evidentiary claim to the 5 piloted branches, or add data/argument showing the non-pilot branches are comparable.
findings.violation: The pilot data only covers 5 branches, but the recommendation extends to all 10 consortium branches without any argument for why the other 5 (non-pilot) branches would behave the same way.

findings.evidence: "items still unreturned past that window remain subject to the existing replacement-cost billing process, matching the return-rate pattern the pilot data actually established"
findings.fix: Either cite the specific pilot data (e.g., percentage of eventual returns completed within 60 days) that justifies this cutoff, or remove the claim that it matches the pilot pattern.
findings.violation: No 60-day threshold or related breakdown appears anywhere in the pilot data described earlier, so the claim that this cutoff "matches the return-rate pattern the pilot data actually established" is unsupported by anything presented in the document.

findings.evidence: "The systems team plans to update the online catalog's fine-display field during the same rollout window."
findings.fix: Replace this sentence with an actual argument or data for systemwide applicability (e.g., comparison of branch demographics, patron behavior across all 10 branches), or move this sentence to an implementation/logistics section.
findings.location: Why the Pilot Result Applies Systemwide, first line
findings.violation: This sentence is an IT scheduling note, not a reason the pilot's results would generalize systemwide; the section heading promises a justification that the content never delivers.

findings.evidence: "This is simply how patron behavior works, and no library that has tried it has ever found otherwise."
findings.fix: Remove this claim or replace it with cited evidence from other libraries/consortia that have eliminated fines systemwide.
findings.location: Why the Pilot Result Applies Systemwide, second line
findings.violation: This is an unsupported sweeping generalization with no citation or evidence, asserted as if self-evidently true.

findings.evidence: "The branch renovation project remains on schedule for completion next spring."
findings.fix: Replace this sentence with an actual response to the funding shortfall (e.g., alternative revenue source, budget reallocation plan, or data showing fines were a minor revenue contributor).
findings.location: Addressing the Revenue Concern, final paragraph
findings.violation: This sentence does not address the skeptic's stated concern about losing materials-replacement funding; the section heading promises a response to the revenue shortfall but none is given.
